display.purpose: The one sentence at the top of the home page; a step smaller on info pages.

subtitle.purpose: Card titles, list group heads, principles.

lede.purpose: The plain promise under a heading, in text-2, max 58ch.

body.purpose: Everything else. Prose is capped at 68ch.

label.purpose: The small name above a group of things. Sentence case, no tracking.

mono.purpose: Values: passwords, counts, bits, dates, step numbers, keys, the bytes counter.

display-ar.purpose: Arabic headlines in Readex Pro: a step smaller, taller line-height, no letter-spacing.

body-ar.purpose: Arabic text in Readex Pro at 16.5px and 1.75.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Things that float over the page: the Tools menu, search palette, toast, sign-in card, and the first panel of a tool where it overlaps the stage.

shadows.name: shadow-lg-on-ink
shadows.purpose: The same role on the stage and in the dark theme.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: A field that has focus, with an accent edge.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Strong ease-out: things arrive. The default for everything.

motion.name: ease-io
motion.purpose: Things that move across the screen: the icon and title travelling between pages.

motion.name: spring
motion.purpose: A small overshoot for things you set yourself: the pin star.

motion.name: hero-entrance
motion.value: headline 700ms; lede 600ms +90ms; ways in 600ms +170ms; password 550ms +230ms; counter 500ms +520ms; glass scale 0.94 to 1 over 1100ms +60ms
motion.purpose: The one choreographed entrance, on the home page only.

motion.name: glass-spring
motion.value: response 0.55s; damping 1 at rest, 0.74 to 0.82 after a drag or a dropped file
motion.purpose: The glass: turns toward the pointer, follows a drag 1:1 and springs back with the speed it was given.

motion.name: glass-takeover
motion.value: 10 unseen frames averaging under 22ms, then a 400ms fade over the still
motion.purpose: The live canvas replaces the still picture only on machines that keep up.

motion.name: page-change
motion.value: 220ms cross-fade; 400ms for the travelling icon and title

motion.name: idle
motion.purpose: After this the page is idle: the glass stops drawing and repeating CSS motion pauses.

narrative.overview:
Your device is a sealed block of glass: light gets in, your files never get out. The home page shows that with one real object, a slab of optical glass with a page sealed inside it, drawn live by a hand-written shader, and then hands over the working tool. Everything else on the site is quiet on purpose, so the glass is the only thing that shines.

The site is built from two materials. The first is ink: a near-black stage that carries the header, the top of every page, the footer and the maker's promise, in the light theme and the dark theme alike. The second is paper: the bright surface the tools sit on, made of white panels with one hairline edge each. In the dark theme the paper becomes ink panels; the stage does not change. Colour is rationed. Rose, mint and blue are the three lines a prism splits light into, and they appear where light passes through the glass, in the brand mark, and to mark a state. They are never a background wash and never a glow.

The interface is dense and exact: tight grotesque headlines, mono for anything that is a value, 44px controls, hairlines instead of boxes inside boxes. It moves once, when the home page arrives, and after that only when you move something yourself.
keyCharacteristics: One ink stage in both themes; paper (light) or ink panels (dark) for the working areas.
One live 3D object, the glass on the home page. No other page has a scene.
Three spectral colours, kept for the glass, the brand mark and state.
Hairline panels, flat at rest. Shadows only under things that float over the page.
Large tight headlines whose second half is dimmer, never coloured.
Mono for values: passwords, counts, bits, dates, file sizes, keyboard keys.
A real, measured "bytes sent from this page" counter as the proof of the promise.
English and Arabic are both first-class; the Arabic hero is mirrored, not translated in place.

rules.name: The Stage Rule
rules.body: The header, the top of every page, the promise band and the footer are ink in both themes. The styles do this by re-scoping the tokens on those regions, so a component placed on the stage picks up its on-ink colours without a second set of rules. A new region joins the stage by taking the `ink` class, not by hard-coding dark colours.

rules.name: The Spectrum Rule
rules.body: Rose, mint and blue belong to the glass, the brand mark and state. They are never a gradient wash, a glow, a card tint or a category colour. The one place they describe data instead of state is the live password, where they tell symbols and digits apart.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Paper Rule
rules.body: The one thing to do is ink on paper and paper on ink (`--btn-bg` / `--btn-ink`). The primary action is never blue and never coloured.

rules.name: The Dimmer Half Rule
rules.body: Emphasis in a heading is the opposite of emphasis: the second half of the sentence is set in `dim`. It is a flat colour, never a gradient, and it is used only at headline sizes, where its contrast (above 3:1) is enough.

rules.name: The One Voice in Arabic Rule
rules.body: Arabic pages set headings and text in Readex Pro, with letter-spacing forced to zero everywhere so letters join, a 16.5px body at 1.75, and headlines a step smaller with taller line-height for the marks. Values stay in Geist Mono and left to right; the brand name stays in Latin, in Funnel Display.

rules.name: The Value Rule
rules.body: If a visitor could copy it or compare it, it is in mono.

rules.name: The Float Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the thing is over something else. If it sits in the page, it gets a hairline.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: Nothing glows and nothing is blurred. The only light on the site is drawn inside the glass.

dos: Do open every page on the ink stage and put the working tool on paper below it. Add the `ink` class to a band that should join the stage.
Do use the tokens in `01-tokens.css` for every colour, radius and shadow, so the stage re-scoping and the dark theme keep working.
Do keep the primary action ink on paper or paper on ink, one per view.
Do dim the second half of a headline with `dim`, at headline sizes only.
Do set values in Geist Mono with tabular numerals.
Do separate lists with hairlines; use a panel only for an object.
Do pair every status colour with words or an icon.
Do keep tap targets at least 44px and fields at least 16px on touch screens.
Do build with logical properties and check the page in Arabic; mirror directional arrows.
Do keep the glass on its still picture wherever motion is reduced or the machine is slow, and record where any new raster comes from in `docs/provenance/`.
donts: Don't use rose, mint or blue as a background wash, a gradient, a glow, a card tint or a category colour.
Don't set headline emphasis in a gradient or an accent colour.
Don't add a second live scene, or a 3D library. The glass is the only one.
Don't give a panel a shadow unless it floats over something.
Don't blur backgrounds or add glows.
Don't add letter-spacing to Arabic, or set it in a second family.
Don't animate content in on scroll, or leave anything moving while the page sits idle.
Don't invent proof. There are no testimonials or user counts; the proof is the counter and the working tools.
Don't hard-code dark colours for something on the stage.
